## Overview

FADS estimates Cox regression coefficients under two-phase failure-time-auxiliary-dependent sampling, when an expensive covariate is measured only in a validation subsample. The following example generates synthetic data.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(FADS)
library(survival)
set.seed(123)
N <- 1500L
X <- rnorm(N)
Z <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)
W <- X + rnorm(N, sd = 0.8)
T <- rexp(N, rate = exp(log(2) * X - 0.5 * Z))
C <- runif(N, 0, 0.5)
d <- data.frame(time = pmin(T, C), status = as.integer(T <= C), X, Z, W)
s <- fads_design(d, "time", "status", "W", "X",
                 n_srs = 300, n_corner = 5, seed = 123)
fit <- fads(Surv(time, status) ~ X + Z, s,
            expensive = "X", auxiliary = "W",
            bandwidth_method = "stratum")
coef(fit)
```

The estimator treats expensive-covariate values in nonvalidation subjects as unavailable. Use `fads_bootstrap()` to estimate a covariance matrix, noting that bootstrap inference can be computationally expensive.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit_boot <- fads_bootstrap(fit, B = 30)
summary(fit_boot)
```

For checkpointed Monte Carlo calibration, use the scripts in `inst/validation/`. The simulation results reported in the README are from a separate 100-cohort research validation and are not recalculated during vignette builds.
